html:
The Battle of Cuito Cuanavale was fought in southeastern Angola from late 1987 to March 1988 between Angolan and Cuban forces on one side and South African troops and UNITA on the other.

It began with an Angolan offensive against UNITA, which South African forces stopped on the Lomba river. They then besieged the Angolan base at Cuito Cuanavale, but repeated attacks failed against defenders reinforced by Cuba.

Both sides claimed victory. The stalemate, and a Cuban advance toward the Namibian border, pushed South Africa to sign the agreements of December 1988, by which Cuban troops left Angola and South Africa left Namibia. Castro and later Mandela hailed it as a turning point against apartheid. It was the largest clash of the Angolan Civil War.
sum: The Battle of Cuito Cuanavale was fought in southeastern Angola from late 1987 to March 1988 between Angolan and Cuban forces on one side and South African troops and UNITA on the other.
